subject: Post-call recap: GridWare deployment topology, SLA & model requirements
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@gridware.com>; Olivia Chen <olivia@gridware.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: GridWare deployment topology, SLA & model requirements

Thanks again for taking time this morning — quick recap and clear next steps so we keep momentum. High-level from our side: we heard three primary goals and constraints from GridWare during the call:

- Goal: Replace latency-sensitive inference path in the customer chat product with an LLM-backed answer assistant while holding P95 token latency under ~120–150ms during peak hours.
- Pain: Current spikes during daytime peaks; bursty QPS (short bursts of several hundred qps) are causing tail latency violations today.
- Compliance: SOC 2 controls required; at minimum, audit logs and encrypted-at-rest request stores. Data residency currently US-only, but you mentioned EU evaluation for next year.

Technical notes / asks we agreed on:
1) Target performance SLOs: please confirm target P95 token latency and an objective for cold-start vs warmed KV cache. We recommended P95 < 150ms initial target; GridWare prefers < 120ms if feasible.
2) Workload profile: peak and baseline QPS, typical prompt length (in tokens), and % of multimodal/embedded requests.
3) Model accuracy bar: clarify top-1 acceptance criteria vs fallbacks (we discussed an option to degrade to a smaller model when we hit capacity/failover).
4) Security checklist: SOC 2 scope, encryption/KMS preference, and whether you need private deployment (VPC) vs Redwood Dedicated.

Attachments: call-recording-20271107.mp3, initial-sizing-estimate.xlsx (rough first-pass sizing from the call).

Proposed immediate next steps (owners):
- GridWare (Samir): share peak/baseline QPS metrics and 24-72 hour latency traces (action: Samir, by Tue 11/9).
- Redwood (Marcus + Neha): propose a topology sketch and expected P95 by model family (action: Marcus, by Wed 11/10).
- Both: schedule an ops deep-dive to validate KV cache expectations and fallback policies (I’ll send a Calendly invite).

If that all looks right, I’ll treat Marcus’s topology diagram as the working draft for the deep-dive.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.inference
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: GridWare deployment topology, SLA & model requirements

Thanks, Mina — great summary. A few clarifications and I've attached the latency traces you asked for (gridware_latency_trace.csv).

Quick answers:
- Peak burst observed last week: ~600 qps (durations of ~3–6 minutes, several times per day). Baseline: 40–70 qps.
- Average prompt length (tokens): ~45 tokens; 95th percentile prompt length ~220 tokens due to some long-form summaries.
- Accuracy: our internal metric is top-1 accuracy on domain dataset should be >= 88% vs current baseline. If we must fallback to a smaller model temporarily, we need the option to mark outputs as “probabilistic” for UI handling.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II in progress; audit logs are required. For now, US residency only.

I've attached gridware_latency_trace.csv — it contains a 72-hour trace with p50/p95/p99 per minute. Happy to jump on the deep-dive.

—Samir

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: GridWare deployment topology, SLA & model requirements

Thanks for the trace, Samir — useful signals. High-level technical read and a proposed topology (attached as proposed-topology-diagram.vsdx). Summary follows; we should validate these assumptions in the ops deep-dive:

Assumptions gathered from the trace and call:
- Short bursty peaks (~600 qps) with median prompt ~45 tokens and tail prompts up to ~220 tokens.
- Goal: operational P95 token latency <= 120–150ms under typical production mix.
- Need for audit logs and encrypted-at-rest storing request/response metadata (Redwood Dedicated / Private options available).

Initial topology recommendation (sketch):
1) Per-region Dedicated GPU pool (US east/west split optional) with weekend autoscaling headroom. Reserve a baseline of GPU nodes sized for 100–150 qps sustained and allow fast burst capacity for the 600 qps peaks.
2) Continuous batching window tuned aggressively (5–25ms) with dynamic batch caps for latency-SLO paths and a separate throughput pool for non-critical jobs.
3) KV cache (prefix caching): warm the cache for frequent prompts; expect cold-starts for ~15% of requests initially. Plan for server-side KV persistence to reduce warm-up penalties.
4) Model variants + fallback: primary model (open-weights ~70B family quantized to 4-bit) with a lightweight 7B fallback for emergency degradation. Final model selection will depend on quality vs cost tradeoffs during evaluation.
5) Quantization & kernels: recommend 4-bit quantization plus optimized attention kernels; benchmarking will determine exact P95 numbers.

Data & metrics required from GridWare for sizing:
- 72-hour minute-level latency/requests trace (we have the CSV — thanks).
- Distribution of prompt lengths (bins).
- Ratio of generate vs embedding/rerank calls.

Risks & mitigations:
- Cold-start KV penalties — mitigate with progressive pre-warming and short-lived dedicated warm nodes.
- Tail latency from large prompts — we can cap generation length or route long prompts to the throughput pool with async response patterns.

I attached the proposed-topology-diagram.vsdx as a working draft. Next step: schedule the ops deep-dive (30–45m) to walk the diagram, confirm the KV hit-rate assumptions, and agree on an evaluation suite for quality gating.
- Marcus
